prompt: Map an existing semantic token set for a night-shift logistics screen. Operators switch between bright warehouse kiosks, dim phones, and Windows forced-colors. A previous dark mode simply inverted light values and the saved theme preference flashes after load. Preserve alert meaning with text or icons as well as color.
assertions: Creates tuned light, dark, high-contrast, and forced-colors behavior from semantic roles rather than raw-color inversion.
Defines preference precedence and no-flash behavior without suppressing user system settings.
Measures relevant text and UI pairs in each mapping and names recovery for missing source roles.
Hands per-theme accessibility evidence to a11y-pass with status, reason, remediation, evidence, and provenance; bare checkmarks and dishonest n/a fail.
Preserves grounded theme fallback and failure behavior while three runs vary structure, aesthetic treatment, and voice and use one authoritative self-check.

run_protocol.material_difference_requirement: Accept diversity only when each compared run cites at least two material changes across the declared axes and ties each change to the prompt or evidence; a new order, synonym, recolor, or unsupported style swap is not diversity.
run_protocol.negative_routing_requirement: The negative neighbor (color-system) must be explicitly rejected with a reason and handoff boundary.
